evidence: The paper applies and analyzes GraphRAG on the FNS 2023 financial narrative summarization dataset, comparing it to naive RAG and proposing an optimized domain adaptation variant.
The paper proposes an LLM-as-optimizer framework that extends GraphRAG's domain adaptation strategy to improve entity and relation extraction prompts using ground-truth summaries.
Paper defines and operationalizes human-AI synergy as outperforming max(human, AI), reports pooled effect g=-0.23 across 370 effect sizes
Paper operationalizes human augmentation as outperforming human alone, reports pooled effect g=0.64 across 370 effect sizes; distinguishes from synergy
Paper presents a MAC framework for enterprise applications with hierarchical agents, inter-agent communication, payload referencing, and dynamic routing.
The paper's entire analysis is organized around human-AI collaboration as the central construct; it synthesizes 96 factors and three conceptual framings of this concept.
The paper's primary contribution is a multi-angled conceptualization and definition of Agentic AI, including capability comparison tables, autonomy levels, and an evolution narrative from GenAI.
Chain-of-thought reasoning is a central mechanism surveyed; the paper traces CoT from early prompting (Wei et al.) through its evolution into deep reasoning in Agentic AI systems.
RAG is extensively surveyed as the primary memory and knowledge-retrieval mechanism in Agentic AI, with coverage of classic RAG, adaptive RAG, experience-based RAG, and knowledge graph retrieval.
Proposes a novel three-dimensional levels-of-autonomy framework (flexibility, proactivity, supervision) for AI agents in knowledge work
